mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day period of similar rate conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the labor participation rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which increases perceived risk and depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while UNRATE decreases by >0.2 percentage points within the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite the trigger being active.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer confidence (HOUST) exceeds 110 for two consecutive months, it indicates robust demand which accelerates corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 110 and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day average preceding the trigger (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month suggests supply-side shocks that reduce future earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly worse than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) remains below 2% for three consecutive months, it suggests central bank patience, allowing equity discount rates to remain low and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not higher than the 30-day average of the previous 6 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% and a rise in average hourly earnings (not available in the provided proxies - thus this sketch is invalid per the constraints) cannot be constructed. Instead, a labor signal using PAYEMS: when temporary job gains (PAYEMS) exceed 50,000 for two months while UNRATE remains below 4%, it implies labor market expansion that boosts investor confidence and drives positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 for 2 months and UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite the trigger being met.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of accelerating federal funds rate hikes (FEDFUNDS increasing at an increasing pace), the present value of future dividends is discounted more heavily, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: Second derivative of FEDFUNDS monthly changes is positive (accelerating hikes)
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day window of similar rate acceleration (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) shows three consecutive months of double-digit declines, it signals a deepening supply-side recession that reduces earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when the trigger is active.
